ceo_directive_6_response: Transition safety from DEMONSTRATED_IN_MODEL to preclinical validation protocol
purpose: Validate fail-safe architecture (FS1+FS3) and biocompatibility in chronic animal model

test_article_definition.device: eShunt prototype with ePTFE membrane + FS1 bypass + FS3 redundant channel

animal_model.rationale: Ovine CSF dynamics similar to human; accepted by FDA for CSF shunt testing

flow_conditions.implantation: Endovascular deployment via jugular vein to dural venous sinus

fouling_protocol.natural_fouling: Allow CSF protein adsorption over 12 weeks
fouling_protocol.measurement: Weekly MRI to assess membrane patency

failure_injections.expected: Flow decreases, bypass activates at threshold

bypass_testing.FS1_activation: Measure ICP when bypass opens (target: 15±2 mmHg)
bypass_testing.FS3_redundancy: If FS1 fails, does FS3 activate? (target: yes, <30s)
bypass_testing.response_time: ICP threshold to bypass open (target: <1s FS1, <30s FS3)

icp_measurement.data_logged: ICP, CSF pressure, venous pressure, differential, bypass state

acceptance_criteria.target: ≥75% of test animals maintain patency (>50% baseline flow)
Bypass activates at 15±3 mmHg (in vivo tolerance wider)
All ISO 10993 tests pass (no cytotoxicity, sensitization, irritation)
No device-related deaths, infections, or migrations
If FS1 fails, FS3 maintains drainage

statistical_plan.analysis: Fisher's exact test for patency; t-test for ICP; descriptive for bypass

estimated_timeline: 6 months (2 months setup, 3 months in-life, 1 month histology)
regulatory: Requires IACUC approval (institutional animal care and use committee)
